newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schering says eyes takeovers with caution.
newsitem.headline: Schering says eyes takeovers with caution.

text.p: German drugs group Schering AG, fresh from making two large acquisitions in 1996, on Wednesday said it was interested in further takeovers but would be quite careful in assessing its potential future plans.

Asked at a news conference whether Schering would be interested in buying more new companies, the group's chief financial officer Klaus Pohle said, "We would gladly make similar acquisitions like we made with Leiras and Jenapharm and we still have cash in our pockets."

But Pohle and Schering management board chairman Giuseppe Vita added that prices for potential takeover targets were currently too high and that Schering would weigh its options very carefully. "Momentarily the prices are completely out of all relations," Vita said.
On the other hand, Pohle also said Schering would likely not be the target of a hostile takeover attempt as the group's price tag, put at 16.5 billion marks, is considered very high.
"Consequently I say that such rumours about a possible hostile takeover are not extremely well founded," Pohle said.

In 1996, Schering took over Finnish group Leiras and German group Jenapharm from pharmaceutical wholesaler Gehe AG. Both these companies are expected to help Schering increase its turnover in the next years.
